questions.scenario: A returns policy changes every week. The chatbot must answer from the current policy and cite the document.
questions.question: Which approach should you use?

options.text: Retrieval-augmented generation that searches an index refreshed from the policy documents
options.why: Correct. Updating the index updates the answers without retraining.

options.text: Fine-tune the model each week on the new policy
options.why: Fine-tuning is slow and costly, and is not a reliable way to add changing facts.

options.text: Increase the temperature of the model
options.why: Temperature changes variety of wording, not knowledge.

options.text: Raise the max output tokens
options.why: This changes answer length and does not add policy content.

questions.explanation: RAG supplies current facts at query time. Refreshing the index is far cheaper than retraining a model.

questions.scenario: Users search for exact product codes such as KX-4420 and also ask paraphrased questions such as "my kettle stopped heating".
questions.question: Which retrieval method best supports both?

options.text: A full-table scan in the application
options.why: It does not scale and does not rank by relevance.

options.text: Hybrid search that combines keyword and vector queries
options.why: Correct. Keywords catch exact codes and vectors catch meaning.

options.text: Keyword search only
options.why: Keyword search misses paraphrased questions.

options.text: Vector search only
options.why: Vector search can miss exact identifiers.

questions.explanation: Hybrid search merges keyword and vector results, which suits mixed query styles.

questions.scenario: Retrieved chunks often start mid-sentence, and answers lack the surrounding context.
questions.question: What should you adjust in the ingestion process?

options.text: The temperature of the chat model
options.why: Temperature does not change how documents are split.

options.text: The number of projects in the resource
options.why: Projects do not affect chunking.

options.text: The chunk size and overlap
options.why: Correct. Larger chunks or more overlap keep related text together.

options.text: The deployment type of the chat model
options.why: Deployment type affects processing location and billing, not chunk boundaries.

questions.explanation: Chunking decides what the retriever can return. Tune size and overlap and test with real questions.

questions.scenario: A support bot must avoid inventing policy details when retrieval returns nothing useful.
questions.question: Which two actions should you take? Select two.

options.text: Return source identifiers with each chunk so the answer can cite them
options.why: Correct. Citations let users and evaluators check the answer.

options.text: Raise the temperature so the model explores more answers
options.why: A higher temperature increases the chance of invented details.

options.text: Remove the instructions so the model has more freedom
options.why: Removing instructions makes ungrounded answers more likely.

options.text: Instruct the model to answer only from the supplied sources and say it does not know otherwise
options.why: Correct. The instruction sets the behaviour when sources are missing.

questions.explanation: Grounding combines clear instructions with sources that can be cited.

questions.scenario: An index stores vectors created with text-embedding-3-small. Queries return poor matches after a developer embeds the query with a different embedding model.
questions.question: What is the cause?

options.text: Query vectors and index vectors must come from the same embedding model
options.why: Correct. Vectors from different models are not comparable.

options.text: The chat model has too little quota
options.why: The chat model is not involved in vector similarity.

options.text: Hybrid search cannot use vectors
options.why: Hybrid search does combine vectors with keywords.

options.text: The index has too many replicas
options.why: Replicas affect availability and query volume, not relevance of vectors.

questions.explanation: Use the same embedding model for ingestion and for queries.
